title: Space Tech Briefing — July 29, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts, and welcome to your daily dose of the cosmos! It's July 29, 2026, and we're bringing you the very latest and greatest from across the universe and right here on Earth. Let's dive in!

First up, for those of you exploring France this summer, specifically Normandy, get ready for a stellar experience! The CNES is inviting everyone, young and old, to an exciting new exhibition titled "Destination Mars!" This fantastic display celebrates a monumental milestone: the 50th anniversary of the historic Viking missions. It's a fun and engaging journey, tracing half a century of incredible Red Planet exploration. So, if you're in Normandy, make sure to add "Destination Mars!" to your must-see list!

And as we wait for today's new launches, let's look back at a major recent development that has everyone talking. Just a few days ago, on July 24th, SpaceX achieved another spectacular success with Starship Flight 13! This thirteenth test flight confirmed several critical technical objectives. We saw the successful deployment of the first-ever Starlink V3 satellites, a huge step forward for the constellation. The mission also featured an in-flight engine relight and a flawless atmospheric re-entry of the upper stage, culminating in a gentle splashdown right in the Indian Ocean. This flight truly marks a significant leap for the Starship program, validating the powerful Raptor V3 engines in space. The big question now is: will Flight 14 be the one that attempts an orbital mission? We'll be watching closely!

That's all for your morning space briefing on this July 29th. Thank you for tuning in, and keep looking up! We'll be back tomorrow with more exciting news from the final frontier.
